newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl urges SPD to join in tax talks.
newsitem.headline: Kohl urges SPD to join in tax talks.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Wednesday urged the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) to resume tax talks with the government, but did not directly answer an earlier SPD letter setting out conditions for the talks.
"The talks...should be resumed as soon as possible," Kohl said in a letter to SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine. "A date can be agreed in the next few days with the Finance Minister."
Lafontaine had asked Kohl to resume the talks in a letter which his party said was intended as an invitation to a personal discussion betwen the two leaders.

Kohl's reply specifically said the talks should be conducted on the government side by Christian Democrat parliamentary leader Wolfgang Schaeuble, Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Free Democrat parliamentary leader Hermann Otto Solms.
He referred to an SPD negotiating team of parliamentary party leader Rudolf Scharping, Hamburg mayor Henning Voscherau and North Rhine-Westphalia state finance minister Heinz Schleusser.
"Kohl is chickening out," said an SPD spokeswoman, without specifying whether the SPD was prepared to resume talks even if Kohl was not present.
